correctness.rationale: The standard 1-WL/C² depth bridge says D^2_#(G)=R(G)+1. Uniform round-zero separates graph order and degree round-one forces two degree-one vertices and all other degree-two vertices; hence surviving nonisomorphic rivals are a single P_m plus one or more disjoint cycles. Color propagation from endpoints maintains identical histograms until round floor(m/2), after which the shorter path center sees meeting fronts, distinguishing at floor(m/2)+1. Since each cycle requires at least 3 vertices, maximum m=n−3, yielding R(P_n)=floor((n−1)/2) for n≥5; small n=1..4 independently handled. Corrected independent joint-color refinement replay checked all P_m∪C_(n−m) rivals for n=5..14; proof is for arbitrary cycle decompositions and n.
residual_risks: Round-zero versus round-one conventions must be respected; the off-by-one distinction is explicit.
Computational checks handle a subset of cycle partitions; general multi-cycle result follows analytic wavefront argument.
